title: WATCH: Philippines sees no threat from AI, says Lazaro
summary: The DFA chief's remarks come amid protests against Pax Silica, a US-led initiative involving semiconductor and AI supply chains.

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Philippines does not consider artificial intelligence a threat and is eager to explore its potential, Foreign Affairs Secretary Theresa Lazaro said Monday, November 16, as Southeast Asian leaders discussed a South Korean proposal for AI cooperation.
"AI is not a threat. That's the Philippine position. We're looking forward to know more about AI," Lazaro said after a press briefing on the second day of the 49th ASEAN Summit in Manila.
Lazaro was responding to a question about South Korea's proposed AI initiative, which was discussed during the summit between the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) and South Korea.
She said discussions had taken place but the details of the proposed initiative had yet to be "fleshed out."
Her remarks came amid protests against Pax Silica, a separate US-led initiative aimed at securing global semiconductor and AI supply chains.
Protesters have raised concerns over the proposed initiative ahead of US President Donald Trump's scheduled arrival in the Philippines on Tuesday, Nov. 17.
